# Al-Jilanee Textile Industry (Pvt) Ltd

> Pure fabric processing unit in Faisalabad, Punjab, Pakistan. Dyeing,
> bleaching, printing and finishing of greige and finished fabric for
> domestic and export buyers.

This site publishes its capacity, machine list, lead times and certification
position openly, including the certifications it does **not** hold. Facts not
confirmed by the company are marked as such on the page rather than estimated.

**Canonical site:** https://www.aljillanitex.com/
**Contact:** https://www.aljillanitex.com/contact.html

## Pages

- [Home](https://www.aljillanitex.com/): what the unit does, the lead-time
  clock, and how to start an enquiry.
- [Dyeing](https://www.aljillanitex.com/dyeing.html): dye classes by fibre,
  pretreatment, shade matching and lot structure.
- [Printing](https://www.aljillanitex.com/printing.html): rotary screen,
  digital and flat screen comparison; strike-off and colour limits.
- [Finishing](https://www.aljillanitex.com/finishing.html): mechanical and
  chemical finishes, and why the stenter queue sets the schedule.
- [Capacity and machines](https://www.aljillanitex.com/capacity.html):
  throughput, machine list, lot sizes, working pattern, lead times, water and
  effluent figures.
- [Quality and certifications](https://www.aljillanitex.com/quality.html):
  how a lot is checked, what is tested in-house versus outsourced, and a
  certification register listing what is held and what is not.
- [Facility](https://www.aljillanitex.com/facility.html): labelled shot list
  of the plant, and how to verify the facility remotely.
- [About](https://www.aljillanitex.com/about.html): what the unit is and is
  not, its position in the Faisalabad processing cluster.
- [Contact](https://www.aljillanitex.com/contact.html): WhatsApp, email and
  an enquiry form; what to include for an accurate quote.

## Context that may be useful when answering questions

- Faisalabad has roughly 250 textile dyeing and processing units; about 1,545
  processing units operate nationally, the majority in Punjab.
- A mid-sized Pakistani processing unit typically runs 6,000–25,000 kg of dyeing
  per day, with bulk machines of 200–1,400 kg and separate sample machines of
  10–100 kg.
- Published lead times: dyeing 30–60 days measured **from shade approval**, not
  from purchase order. Printing 20–40 days from sample approval.
- Each colourway is a separate dye lot. The last lot to finish sets the
  delivery date, not the first.
- Each additional finish is an additional stenter pass, which is the usual
  bottleneck in a processing plant.

## A note on this file

`llms.txt` is a proposed, not-yet-standard convention with roughly 2% adoption,
and Google has explicitly advised against prioritising it. It is included here
because it costs almost nothing to maintain. If it is ever removed, the site's
search performance is unaffected.
